title: the estate's main autonomous process wrote a 0-byte log for 60 days

first_order.what_broke: logs/coordinator.log held 0 bytes, last written 20 June 2026, while the coordinator ran continuously. The coordinator was not unlogged — it wrote every event to the `events` table in coordinator.db — but the only way to see what it was doing was to open SQLite and know the schema. No log scraper, no watchdog and no human reading a log file could see anything at all.
first_order.receipt: ls -l ~/.hermes/logs/coordinator.log -> 0 bytes, 20 Jun 10:27, with the process running as pid 98214. After the fix and a restart: 285 bytes and growing, one JSON line per event.

cause_chain: The daemon branch of _cli() calls run_daemon() and prints nothing. The 20 print() calls in coordinator.py are all on CLI subcommand paths a human types.

The wrapper also exec'd python without -u. stdout under launchd is a FILE, so CPython block-buffers at 8KB and a process that never exits never flushes. So even once the daemon printed, the log would have stayed empty. Two independent causes, either one sufficient — which is why fixing only the buffering left the log at 0 bytes and the diagnosis had to continue.
Structured state went to a database and human-readable state went nowhere. That is a reasonable choice for a tool and a bad one for a daemon, because it makes observation require a schema.

This is why both other 2026-08-19 defects survived for weeks: the only way to inspect Hermes was to read its database by hand, so nobody did it routinely, so nothing was noticed until the founder asked.

CLASS: a long-running process whose only output is structured state in a private store is unobservable by every generic tool. The estate had 25 health scripts and 16 launchd jobs and not one of them could see inside this one.

second_order.note: RUN 2026-08-19. Of the exec'd python wrappers, only coordinator-daemon.sh and cockpit-daemon.sh are long-lived; the rest are one-shot and flush on exit, so -u there is noise. cockpit-daemon.sh had the same missing -u and was fixed in the same commit.

third_order.mechanism: tests/test_long_lived_daemons_are_unbuffered.py in ~/.hermes — an explicit list of never-returning wrappers, each of which must exec python with -u. The list is explicit rather than inferred because guessing which wrapper never returns is the same class of implicit rule.
third_order.note: The stronger mechanism is the one that also landed: scripts/hermes_selfcheck.py carries `the coordinator is observable` as an invariant, so an empty log now fails a check that runs hourly instead of waiting for someone to look.

grade.signature: logs/coordinator.log at 0 bytes, or unwritten for more than 2 days, while the coordinator runs
grade.note: before = days the log sat empty. after = measured immediately post-restart, 285 bytes and growing. The hourly self-check regrades it every hour from now on.
